meta.note: written five weeks into 2026 from the standings, the all-play Elo, the season simulation's odds, each roster's WAR pace (banked plus the rest of the projection, best legal lineup, taxi and IR excluded), and every trade since the preseason outlooks

8.head: 5-0 · Elo 1698 (1st) · WAR pace +9.76 (1st) · playoffs 99.8% · title 36%
8.text: The all-in bet is paying. Five wins, the most points in the league, and first in Elo and in WAR pace, with every one of the nine seats on pace for a positive season. Jared Goff and Bryce Young are outscoring the plan at quarterback, CeeDee Lamb, Amon-Ra St. Brown and Brock Bowers are doing what they were bought to do, and all five wins came by 14 points or more. The risk has not changed since August: no first or second before 2029, so an injury has to be covered from the roster. The roster can cover it. Jayden Daniels is on the bench at 0.84, and a starting superflex quarterback sitting unused is the best trade chip any contender holds. Flipping him for a real flex upgrade over Chase Brown is the one move that makes a 36% title favorite bigger.

2.head: 4-1 · Elo 1664 (2nd) · WAR pace +9.32 (2nd) · playoffs 99.1% · title 36%
2.text: Second in everything, and the only loss was the 214-point week from the team in first. Bijan Robinson is on pace for the best running back season on the roster and Lamar Jackson, Christian McCaffrey and Isaiah Likely are carrying the rest. The preseason worry was the WR2 and WR3 seats, and they got filled by Davante Adams and Mike Evans, both 33, with Travis Kelce at 36 in the flex. That is the oldest lineup in the league at 29.3 and it is working this year, which is the only year it was built for. Saquon Barkley came in for Brian Thomas and a 2027 second and is on the bench at 0.25, so the deal has not paid yet. With no first or second left in 2027, the 2028 first is the last real chip. Spend it on youth at receiver, not on another 30-year-old.

10.head: 4-1 · Elo 1564 (7th) · WAR pace +6.86 (5th) · playoffs 91% · title 6%
10.text: The record is better than the team. Third in points for, fifth in WAR pace and seventh in Elo, which means the schedule has done some of the work, and the season simulation still has this as a 91% playoff team with a 6% title shot. Derrick Henry at 32 was the preseason sell and he is instead the banked WAR leader at 0.56, so holding him was right for now. Kyren Williams, Garrett Wilson and Tyler Warren are pulling their weight. Jaylen Waddle at 0.20 in the WR3 seat and Tucker Kraft at 0.37 in the flex are the soft spots, and four players on IR with Bo Nix questionable leaves no depth behind them. The 2028 and 2029 firsts plus an extra 2028 second are enough to buy one receiver. That buys a bye; standing pat buys a first-round exit.

6.head: 3-2 · Elo 1636 (3rd) · WAR pace +7.62 (3rd) · playoffs 85% · title 8%
6.text: Third in Elo and third in WAR pace on a 3-2 record, and the gap between this team and the top two is a hospital report. De'Von Achane is on IR, and Dak Prescott, George Kittle, Bucky Irving, Rashee Rice and Ladd McConkey all carry tags. The preseason note said cash something, and they did: a 2028 first and a 2027 third for Irving, a fair price for a 24-year-old back. Christian Watson has been the surprise, leading the roster in banked WAR. The number to fix is 171: the gap between points scored and the best possible lineup, the second biggest in the league and the biggest for any contender. With this much injury churn, setting the lineup is the cheapest upgrade there is. An 85% playoff team that gets Achane back in December is as dangerous as anyone.

9.head: 3-2 · Elo 1570 (6th) · WAR pace +6.82 (6th) · playoffs 67% · title 3%
9.text: Jahmyr Gibbs is the best player in the league so far: 0.89 WAR banked and on pace for 2.19, both the highest of anyone. He is also most of the team. Nico Collins and D'Andre Swift are solid, and after that the lineup is Matthew Stafford at 38, Justin Herbert below replacement through five weeks, Dallas Goedert at 31 and Rhamondre Stevenson, who came over with two seconds for Emeka Egbuka. This roster leaves the fewest points on its bench of anyone, only 65 under its best lineup, so the 3-2 is honest and so is sixth in Elo. Every own first through 2029 is still here, plus three extra seconds. That is the best war chest of any team in the playoff picture, and a 67% team with Gibbs is the one that should use it now, at quarterback.

11.head: 3-2 · Elo 1586 (4th) · WAR pace +6.49 (7th) · playoffs 68% · title 3%
11.text: Still three stars and six holes. Jaxon Smith-Njigba is having a monster year, with 0.75 WAR banked and on pace for 1.81, third in the league behind Gibbs and Josh Allen, and Jonathan Taylor and Jalen Hurts are doing their part. Then the superflex seat is Jacoby Brissett at 33, the flex is Hunter Henry at 0.07, Terry McLaurin is a WR3 at 0.16 and T.J. Hockenson has been a quarter of a win. Fourth in Elo says the scores have been better than the roster, and 155 points left on the bench says the lineup could have been better still. The 2028 and 2029 firsts are intact. One trade for a real WR2 turns a 68% coin flip into a lock; without one this is the 7-7 team it was projected to be.

1.head: 2-3 · Elo 1571 (5th) · WAR pace +7.21 (4th) · playoffs 69% · title 7%
1.text: The best 2-3 team in the league by a distance. The three losses came by 4.6, 4.4 and 5.8 points, the roster is fourth in WAR pace and fifth in Elo, and the simulation gives it better playoff and title odds than three of the teams above it in the standings. Brock Purdy and Trey McBride are on pace for the best quarterback and tight end seasons on any contender, and Drake Maye is holding the superflex seat. The bill for the preseason push is on IR: A.J. Brown, bought with the 2027 first, has not helped, and Travis Etienne is out too. Justin Jefferson at 0.73 and Stefon Diggs at 0.17 are the receivers in the meantime, and Mark Andrews in the flex is close to nothing. The record will catch up to the roster.

7.head: 2-3 · Elo 1408 (8th) · WAR pace +3.57 (9th) · playoffs 9% · title 0%
7.text: Josh Allen is on pace for the best quarterback season in the league Joe Burrow is a solid second at 1.05, and this is still a 9% playoff team. The other seven seats combine for under a win, with Kalif Raymond and Adonai Mitchell below replacement and the running back room at roughly zero. Jadarian Price and Jonah Coleman are both on IR, so the rookie class has not had a chance to help. That leaves a decision rather than a lineup problem. Two elite quarterbacks in superflex are the most liquid assets in the league, and at least three contenders, The Hurt Locker, Captain Jah'Merica and Homie G Slicer, have a hole at the second quarterback seat. Allen at 30 is worth more right now than he ever will be to a team without a receiver corps. Selling one of them for a first and a young receiver is how this roster stops wasting them.

3.head: 2-3 · Elo 1394 (9th) · WAR pace +4.96 (8th) · playoffs 12% · title 0%
3.text: Ninth in points, ninth in Elo, and the superflex problem from August is still the story. The second quarterback seat went from Malik Willis to Aaron Rodgers at 42, with Cam Ward and Willis on the bench at about 0.4 each. Kenneth Walker is the bright spot at 0.61 banked, and Patrick Mahomes is solid but questionable. Colston Loveland has been below replacement and Kenyon Sadiq is behind him, so two first-round tight ends have produced nothing yet. A 12% playoff team should stop spending on this season. The good news is the cupboard: Bijan al-Gaib's 2027 first, four seconds across 2027 and 2028, and every own first. Bijan al-Gaib is a contender, so that pick lands late. The offseason job is the same as the August one, a young quarterback, and these picks are enough to buy one.

12.head: 1-4 · Elo 1351 (10th) · WAR pace +1.70 (11th) · playoffs 0.03% · title 0%
12.text: The preseason note said Saquon Barkley had to be flipped or the return would evaporate. He was flipped in September, to Bijan al-Gaib for Brian Thomas and a 2027 second, and then Bucky Irving went to Jeantrification for a 2028 first. That is a rebuild being run on purpose. The pick haul is now two 2027 firsts, Jeantrification's 2028 first and two extra 2027 seconds. The lineup is what it looks like: Jaxson Dart is the only seat on pace for more than half a win, and Jordyn Tyson, Jayden Higgins and Tank Dell are on IR with Christian Kirk. Thomas at 23 has been below replacement so far, which makes him a buy-low the team already owns. 1-4 with an 11th-best roster is the honest result, and the picks are where the value is. Keep collecting.

4.head: 1-4 · Elo 1300 (11th) · WAR pace +2.08 (10th) · playoffs 0.2% · title 0%
4.text: The teardown is on schedule. Four 2027 firsts, own plus Jeantrification's, St. Brown Catholic Church's and The Hurt Locker's, with two of those likely to land late because those teams are winning. The roster is doing what a teardown roster does: Trevor Lawrence, Chris Olave and Tyler Shough are the only seats producing, and both running back seats are below replacement, Justice Hill at -0.52 and Mike Washington at -0.56. Carnell Tate has been quiet as a rookie and Omar Cooper is on IR. The one move of the season was a 2027 second for Caleb Douglas, a young receiver who has not played his way into anything yet. There is nothing to fix this year. The 2027 draft is the plan, and a quarterback with one of those firsts is the move that matters most.

5.head: 0-5 · Elo 1257 (12th) · WAR pace +0.88 (12th) · playoffs 0% · title 0%
5.text: Winless, last in points and last in Elo, which is the expected cost of the plan. The one in-season move cut against it: Rhamondre Stevenson and two seconds went out for Emeka Egbuka, a 23-year-old receiver, which fits the timeline even though Egbuka has been near replacement so far. Marvin Harrison is on IR, Jeremiyah Love is on pace for 0.29 as a rookie, and Fernando Mendoza has not started. The rest of the lineup is Geno Smith, Sam Darnold, Darren Waller and Mike Gesicki, placeholders by design. The value is the draft: four 2027 firsts, including this team's own, which is on track for the top pick, plus three 2028 firsts and the 2029. Nothing on the field this year matters as much as that pick. Patience is the whole job until April.
